picks.excerpt: University at Buffalo researchers paired Raman spectroscopy with a neural network to identify four organelles inside living cells at about 90% accuracy, with no fluorescent dyes. The dye-free 'Ramanomics' route removes a long-standing obstacle to watching cells without perturbing them.
picks.rationale: Concrete method advance: a neural net removes the dye step that has distorted live-cell imaging for decades.

picks.excerpt: Two physicists, one of them a Nobel laureate, cracked a decade-old puzzle about jamming transitions with help from Claude. The account is a concrete look at how an AI model slots into a working theory-physics collaboration rather than replacing it.
picks.rationale: A first-hand account of where an LLM actually fits inside a theory-physics workflow, not a benchmark claim.

picks.excerpt: KAIST built a programmable dynamic memtransistor that retunes its own response speed to match time-series data arriving at different rates. Prediction errors dropped up to 40-fold against fixed-response devices.
picks.rationale: Hardware-side novelty with a hard number: self-retuning device timing cuts time-series prediction error 40-fold.

picks.excerpt: After eight years, 200 million predictions and a Nobel Prize, Google DeepMind has dissolved its dedicated AlphaFold team. The lab argues the problem is largely solved and outside researchers are already carrying the work forward.
picks.rationale: Structural news for AI-in-science: the flagship protein-folding effort is declared done and handed to the field.

picks.excerpt: Emory and Georgia Tech researchers built CapuchinAI, a field system combining facial recognition with touchscreen cognitive tasks for wild capuchin monkeys. It identified individual monkeys with 97% accuracy in Costa Rica, moving primate cognition testing out of the lab.
picks.rationale: Moves an entire experimental paradigm out of the lab into the wild, widening the topical spread beyond physics and chips.
